subject: Hosted API: Data Locality & Retention Interrogatory
messages:
From: Ivy Reynolds <ivy.reynolds@finedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finedge.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: Data locality & retention interrogatory

Hi Mina / Marissa,

Thanks for taking our questionnaire. As part of FinEdge's security review we're collecting precise answers on where customer data (prompts, responses, logs, backups, and KV/cache) lives, how long it's retained, and how deletion is enforced for Hosted API customers. Below is a short set of questions — can you provide concise answers we can attach to our vendor risk record?

1) For Redwood Hosted API: which physical regions (cloud regions / countries) may store the following items by default: a) API request/response payloads, b) model-only artifacts (weights/quantized blobs), c) short-term KV/cache used for inference, d) system logs and audit logs, e) backups/snapshots?
2) What are default retention TTLs (hours/days) for request/response payloads, KV/cache, logs, and backups?
3) When a customer requests erasure (account delete + data purge), what is the expected end-to-end timeline for removing: a) active request/response records, b) cached KV/prefix entries, c) backups/snapshots and their offsite copies?
4) Do backups replicate across regions by default? If so, what controls exist to prevent cross-jurisdiction replication for customers requiring geo-bound data?
5) Are all stored customer artifacts encrypted at rest and in transit? Please call out KMS ownership (Redwood-managed vs. customer-managed) options for Hosted API.
6) Any exceptions where data may be retained longer (legal holds, billing, debug traces)? If yes, what is the process to request an exception or to provide attestation?

We appreciate short, direct answers (bullets are fine). If there are attachments you can point us to for evidence (architectural diagram, retention matrix, SOC2 artifact), please include them.

Best,
Ivy Reynolds
Senior InfoSec Manager
FinEdge

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ivy Reynolds <ivy.reynolds@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Data locality & retention interrogatory

Hi Ivy — thanks for the clear list. Answering inline with concise bullets and attaching a short evidence pack. If you want, we can hop on a 30m call to walk the architecture.

High-level summary (Hosted API, default behavior):
- Regions: by default, customer request/response payloads and inference KV/cache are colocated in the cloud region that serves the API request (we run in multi-region cloud providers; customers pick region on creation). Model binary artifacts are stored in regional object stores and cached on GPUs; replication policy for model weights is provider/region-specific. System & audit logs are stored in a central logging cluster per region with configurable retention. Backups/snapshots of persistent state are taken per-region.
- Default TTLs: request/response payloads retained for 30 days by default; short-term KV/cache is ephemeral (minutes to hours depending on workload; typical TTLs are 5-60 minutes); system logs retained 90 days; backups retained 30 days unless customer elects longer via a retention contract.
- Erasure timeline: active records and request/response indexes: up to 48 hours for logical deletion, with full physical purging from hot store within 30 days depending on replication and backup cycles. Cached KV/prefix entries expire automatically within configured TTL (minutes→hours). Backups/snapshots: removal initiated within 72 hours and completion depends on backup lifecycle (max 30 days to guarantee eradication from all retention stores).
- Cross-region replication: not replicated across regions by default for customer data; backups are region-bound unless the customer is on a Dedicated or Private plan with explicit cross-region replication.
- Encryption: all customer data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest, data is encrypted using provider-managed keys by default. Hosted API customers can request customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) for selected enterprise contracts — provide KMS ARN and we integrate.
- Exceptions: legal holds and support/forensics requests can pause deletion; such exceptions require documented approval from the customer and are logged. Billing records (aggregates/usage) are retained for accounting and are minimally identifiable; these are retained per our billing policy (up to 3 years with redaction).

Attachments included: hostedapi-data-flow-v2.pdf (diagram), retention-matrix-2026.xlsx (TTL by artifact type), soc2-infra-summary.pdf (controls summary).

Short clarifications: we treat "request payloads" and "generated content" as customer data and subject to erasure requests. Model binaries/weights are not customer-specific and are not removed as part of a customer erasure flow.

If you need RBC (region-bound) attestations or a signed statement, let me know and I can route to Legal for a short SOC/POA.

— Mina Haddad
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ivy Reynolds <ivy.reynolds@finedge.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks Mina — that helps. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) For the 30-day default retention on request/response payloads — can you confirm whether that includes transient debug logs (traces emitted for a single request)? Do those traces follow the 30-day TTL or shorter?
2) For backups: if a customer creates an erasure request on Day 0, are there manual steps required to purge archived backups or does your orchestration automatically schedule deletion across all retention tiers?
3) For BYOK: if we provide a KMS key, is key rotation visible/auditable from our side?

If you can reply with single-line bullets, we can close our assessment.

Ivy

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ivy Reynolds <ivy.reynolds@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Data locality & retention interrogatory

Hi Ivy — quick bullets to close out:  

1) Debug traces: traced events emitted at request time are classified as ephemeral operational traces. Default retention is 7 days; they are excluded from the 30-day request/response retention window unless explicitly enabled by the customer for longer debugging.

2) Backups & erasure: erasure request triggers automated orchestration that: (a) marks active records for deletion immediately, (b) schedules backup rekey/removal jobs and flags snapshots for expedited deletion. If backups are stored in immutable third-party archives beyond our control, we initiate a documented purge workflow and provide an attestation when complete; typical completion time is within 30 days. Manual intervention is rare and logged when needed.

3) BYOK visibility: when a customer supplies a KMS key (BYOK), audit logs (key usage, rotations) are available to the customer via the cloud provider's KMS audit trails. We also surface key usage events in our security console for enterprise customers.

Evidence links: shared Drive folder (see related_links) contains the architecture diagram and retention matrix. If you'd like signed confirmation, Marissa can coordinate a short attestation letter via Legal.

Thanks — happy to schedule a follow-up call.

— Mina
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
